218.body: route() now consults the PSP health table before picking a provider, skipping any provider flagged degraded in the last 5 minutes. Until now it weighted purely by configured share, so a struggling provider kept getting traffic until someone flipped the weights by hand. The health check is a cheap in-memory lookup, and clear() resets the flags for tests. Testing: simulated a degraded provider and confirmed traffic shifts away within a minute.
218.title: payment-router: skip degraded providers in route

219.body: postgres_payments.tf now ships slow-query logs to the central log group with a 500ms threshold. We had zero visibility into which statements were slow on the payments cluster without SSHing into the host. The threshold is deliberately high to keep volume down. No database behavior changes. Testing: ran a slow query on staging and confirmed it appears in the log group.
219.title: postgres-payments: ship slow-query logs to central logging

220.body: Enabled query insights on the payments cluster so the performance dashboard stops being guesswork. one-line change, verified in console.
220.title: postgres-payments: enable query insights

221.body: kafka.tf adds a consumer-lag alarm on the ledger topic that pages the channel when lag passes 10k messages for 5 minutes. The notifications backlog last month sat for an hour before anyone noticed, and this alarm would have caught it in minutes. Threshold picked from the last three months of lag data. Testing: triggered the alarm on staging with a paused consumer.
221.title: kafka: add consumer-lag alarm for the ledger topic

230.body: login() in both app.py and oauth.py now returns the same generic error for unknown users and wrong passwords. The two paths had measurably different response times, which is a textbook user-enumeration signal. AuthService pads the failure path so both look identical. Successful logins are untouched. Testing: timing test asserts both failure modes respond within the same 50ms band.
230.title: auth: normalize login failure responses

231.body: weekend vacuum settings finally sane. autovacuum was waking up every minute and spamming the logs 🙄 set sane thresholds, logs quiet now
231.title: postgres-ledger: calm down autovacuum logging

232.body: reserve() now checks the InStock flag before touching the reservation table, and returns early with a clear 'not stocked' result. Previously every reserve for an unstocked SKU did a full write-then-rollback cycle that showed up as deadlocks under load!! InventoryService callers get the same result shape, just faster. Testing: added unstocked-SKU cases and a small load test showing the deadlocks gone 🎉
232.title: inventory: short-circuit reserve for unstocked SKUs

233.body: ledger backups now run in the 2am window instead of 6pm. was colliding with evening settlement. moved, verified.
233.title: postgres-ledger: move backup window to 2am

234.body: save() in outbox.py now writes the entry and the outbox row in a single transaction, and relay() picks them up in entry order instead of whatever order the poll returns. The old code could publish entry B before entry A after a restart, which confused two consumers. LedgerEntry gains a sequence column, FakeBus.publish asserts ordering in tests, and reset() clears the sequence. Testing: added a restart-ordering test that failed before and passes now.
234.title: ledger: order outbox relay by entry sequence

235.body: The checkout page was fetching the shipping options on every render, including re-renders caused by typing in the address form. render_checkout now memoizes the options by postal code and only refetches when it changes. Typing in the form no longer hammers the endpoint. Testing: typed through the form on staging while watching the network tab — one fetch per postal code.
235.title: web-frontend: memoize shipping options in render_checkout

236.body: Hello — issue_refresh_token will now refuse to mint tokens for clients that have been marked revoked in the registry, returning the standard revoked-client error. Previously a revoked client kept getting fresh tokens until its existing ones expired, which defeats the purpose of revocation. verify_refresh_token already rejected those tokens; this closes the minting side. IdentityService logs revocations at warning level. Testing: added revoked-client cases for both issue and verify paths.
236.title: identity-api: refuse tokens for revoked clients

237.body: dispatch() now matches routes longest-prefix-first instead of registration order, which fixes the /v1/catalog/search shadowing bug that sent search traffic to the catalog handler for a week. check_limit runs after routing so rate-limit buckets follow the matched route, and RateLimited carries the matched route name for debugging. reset() is unchanged. Testing: added shadowing regression tests plus the existing route suite.
237.title: api-gateway: longest-prefix-first routing in dispatch

246.body: test_place_order_empty_cart_fails was asserting the wrong error message after the copy change last month, so it has been red on main for two weeks. Fixed the assertion to match the current copy, and fresh_state now seeds a valid cart so the happy-path test does not depend on test order. test_place_order_confirmation_mentions_order is untouched. Testing: full file green, plus the checkout suite.
246.title: checkout: fix stale assertions in test_place_order

247.body: point-in-time recovery window extended to 7 days. covers the weekend now. applied, verified.
247.title: postgres-payments: extend point-in-time recovery

248.body: capture_payment now validates the amount is positive before calling payments, raising immediately on zero or negative values. A rounding bug upstream sent a $0.00 capture last week and the error came back from deep inside the PSP stack with no context. The validation error names the order and the bad amount. Testing: added zero/negative cases; existing tests unaffected.
248.title: checkout: validate amount in capture_payment

249.body: start_refund now records the reason code on the refund record at creation time instead of in a follow-up write. The two-step version left refunds without reasons whenever the second write failed, and finance chased us monthly. RefundsService validates the reason against the allowed list, and workflow.py passes it through. Testing: added missing-reason regression tests!!
249.title: refunds: persist refund reason at creation

250.body: PaymentRouter startup now validates that the configured provider weights sum to 100 and raises a clear error naming the bad provider. A typo last month gave one provider 80 and another 80, and route() silently normalized instead of complaining. __init__ fails fast now, and route() behavior for valid configs is unchanged. clear() resets weights for tests.
250.title: payment-router: validate provider weights at startup

251.body: AuthService.login now trims whitespace from the email before lookup. Users who copy-paste their email from password managers kept getting 'unknown user' because of a trailing space, and support saw this weekly. The stored email is untouched, only the lookup input is normalized. Testing: added padded-email cases.
251.title: auth: trim email whitespace in login

252.body: start_refund now sends the merchant notification through the template renderer instead of a hardcoded English string. Non-English merchants were getting English emails, which support flagged twice. RefundsService picks the template by merchant locale with English fallback, and workflow.py passes the locale through. Testing: rendered all four supported locales in the test suite.
252.title: refunds: localize merchant refund notifications

253.body: IdentityService now caches registry lookups for 5 minutes instead of hitting the registry on every token request. The registry is slow at peak and token issuance p99 showed it. Stale reads are bounded by the TTL and the registry changes rarely. issue_refresh_token and verify_refresh_token behavior is otherwise unchanged. Testing: added cache-hit tests and confirmed p99 improvement on staging.
253.title: identity-api: cache client registry lookups

254.body: login() in oauth.py handles the provider returning an expired code more gracefully — it now raises a specific expired-code error that the frontend turns into a 'try again' prompt, instead of a generic failure that looked like a bug. No change for valid codes. Testing: replayed an expired code against staging for reimbursement... I mean, for verification.
254.title: auth: handle expired oauth codes in login

255.body: Login rate limiting is now per-IP instead of global. One bad actor locked out everyone last Tuesday. AuthService.login buckets attempts by IP with the same thresholds.
255.title: auth: scope login rate limits per IP

256.body: StripeClient.__init__ now accepts a timeout parameter (default 10s) instead of using the library default of 30s. The 30s default held connections open too long during the provider slowdown. charge() passes the timeout through and raises the same error type on expiry. Testing: simulated a slow provider and confirmed the 10s cutoff!!
256.title: stripe-adapter: configurable timeout in StripeClient

257.body: ledger replica lag alarm added. pages when lag > 30s for 5 min. tested with a stopped replica 📟
257.title: postgres-ledger: add replica lag alarm

258.body: with_retry now stops passing the raw exception object into the log call and instead logs a one-line summary (attempt number, function name, error type). The raw exception repr sometimes included customer email addresses from the payload, which then sat in our logs. MAX_ATTEMPTS and BASE_DELAY are untouched — same behavior, safer logs. Testing: asserted no email addresses appear in log output for the failing cases.
258.title: checkout: scrub PII from with_retry logs

259.body: AuthService.login now supports the 'remember me' flag the frontend shipped last week — it extends the session lifetime instead of ignoring the flag. Previously users who checked the box were still logged out after the default window and filed bugs. The flag flows through to the session store unchanged otherwise. Testing: covered checked, unchecked, and missing-flag cases.
259.title: auth: honor remember-me flag in login

260.body: kafka.tf raises the message size limit on the ledger topic to 2MB. Large settlement batches were getting rejected at the broker. Consumer config unchanged.
260.title: kafka: raise ledger topic message limit

261.body: compaction policy tuned for the events topic. segments were piling up. set size-based cleanup, verified lag flat 🗜️
261.title: kafka: tune compaction on events topic
